Container.Name: jenkins-inbound-agent
Container.Overview:
This is the official Jenkins inbound (JNLP) build agent. The agent dials OUT to your Jenkins controller and connects itself, so no inbound ports need to be opened on this container - ideal for unRAID on your LAN.
DOCKER-CAPABLE VARIANT: this template also lets the agent drive the unRAID host's Docker daemon, so Jenkins pipelines that use the Docker Pipeline plugin (docker.image().inside() / .withRun()) work. That needs THREE things, all wired below: 1. The host Docker SOCKET (/var/run/docker.sock) is mounted so the agent can reach the daemon. 2. The host Docker CLI BINARY (/usr/bin/docker) is mounted read-only - the base image has no docker client, and the socket alone is useless without one. 3. The agent work directory is mapped at the SAME absolute path inside the container and on the host (/mnt/user/appdata/jenkins-inbound-agent/agent). This is REQUIRED for `.inside()`: the plugin bind-mounts the workspace by path against the HOST daemon, so an in-container-only path (e.g. /home/jenkins/agent) would resolve to nothing on the host and the tool container would see an empty workspace. The container runs as root (--user 0:0 in Extra Parameters) so it can use the mounted socket regardless of its permissions. If you prefer least privilege, drop that and instead add `--group-add <gid>` where gid = `stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock` on the host.
https://hub.docker.com/r/jenkins/inbound-agent/
Container.Requires:
1. Create the agent work directory on your array (must match the container path below): mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/jenkins-inbound-agent/agent
2. In Jenkins: Manage Jenkins - Nodes - New Node. Give it a name (this becomes JENKINS_AGENT_NAME below), choose "Permanent Agent", launch method "Launch agent by connecting it to the controller". Set Remote root directory to the SAME path as the work dir: /mnt/user/appdata/jenkins-inbound-agent/agent. Give it the label `docker` if you want it to run Docker Pipeline jobs. Save.
3. Open the node's page. Jenkins shows a connection command containing a -secret hex string. Copy it into JENKINS_SECRET below, and put your controller URL into JENKINS_URL. On the same LAN, use the controller's IP (e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8080), NOT a public/tunnel hostname - tunnels tend to drop long-lived agent WebSockets.
4. Verify Docker works from inside once it starts (use the CONTAINER name, not the Jenkins node name): docker exec jenkins-inbound-agent sh -c 'command -v docker && docker --version && docker ps'
NOTE: if you run a SECOND agent, copy this template but change BOTH the host and container side of "Agent Work Dir" to a new, still-identical path (e.g. /mnt/user/appdata/jenkins-inbound-agent-2/agent), and set that node's Remote root directory to match.

Config.Name: Agent Work Dir
Config.Description: Agent workspace. The host path and the container Target MUST be identical (see Overview) so Docker Pipeline `.inside()` bind-mounts resolve on the host daemon.

Config.Name: Docker Socket
Config.Description: Host Docker daemon socket - lets the agent run Docker Pipeline builds against the host daemon.

Config.Name: Docker CLI Binary
Config.Description: Host docker client binary, mounted read-only. The base image has none; the socket is useless without a client. If `which docker` on your host prints a different path, change the host side to match. (The unRAID docker client is a static Go binary, so it runs inside the agent image as-is.)

Config.Name: Container Variable 3
Config.Description: Must equal the Agent Work Dir Target above.

Config.Name: Jenkins Instance Secret
Config.Description: The -secret hex string from the node's page.

Config.Name: Jenkins URL
Config.Description: Controller URL. On the same LAN use its IP, not a tunnel hostname.

Config.Name: Jenkins Agent Name
Config.Description: Must match the node name you created in Jenkins.
